answer: At the wharf, every paid work slot demands a deposit burned if the job goes undone. One slot costs a 20 POA lock, and an ivory-white mirror registry publishes each claim, so no operator can hide idle slots across many identities. A forger holding 100 slots locks 2,000 POA, and abandoned slots burn their deposits, so the attack costs 2,000 POA while an honest agent pays once and gets it back on delivery. Only finished work opens the next slot.
